raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40155.

The non-overlap scheduler path always calls the spec worker through `forward_batch_generation(batch, pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors)` (`scheduler.py` passes the keyword unconditionally), but the spec-v2 workers drifted apart on this signature and nothing enforced it — `BaseSpecWorker` never declared the method. Each drift only surfaced at the first request as `TypeError: ... got an unexpected keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'`.

**Audit of current main** (the issue's table is from September; two entries were fixed since):

| Worker | `pp_proxy_tensors` |
|---|---|
| `eagle_worker_v2` | ✅ |
| `dflash_worker_v2` | ✅ |
| `ngram_worker` | ✅ |
| `dspark_worker_v2` | ✅ (already fixed on main, #39262) |
| `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2` | ✅ (fixed inline in #29189) |
| `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2` | ❌ **still broken on main** |
| `uno_worker_v2` | ❌ **still broken on main** |

**Relationship to #44211:** that PR was closed unmerged along with all other PRs from its account (closed for a spam pattern of 37 near-duplicate PRs, not for technical reasons). The underlying signature divergence is still unfixed on main, verified today — any FROZEN-KV-MTP or UNO run through the non-overlap path still dies with the TypeError above. This is a fresh, tested take.

## Modifications

- **`frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`** — accept `pp_proxy_tensors` and forward it to the target prefill call and to `self.verify(...)`, exactly matching the `EAGLEWorkerV2` path this worker mirrors and inherits from.
- **`uno_worker_v2.py`** — accept `pp_proxy_tensors`; when it is not None (i.e. pipeline parallelism is active), raise `NotImplementedError`. UNO drives the target model runner directly and never forwards inter-stage proxy tensors, so silently swallowing them — the `del grammar_barrier` treatment — would corrupt a PP run instead of failing. A loud refusal matches the worker's existing style of explicit `NotImplementedError`s for unsupported features.
- **`base_spec_worker.py`** — declare `forward_batch_generation` as an `@abstractmethod` with the full scheduler-facing signature, so the next worker that forgets it fails at instantiation (import time) instead of at the first request.

## Regression Tests

New `test/registered/unit/speculative/test_spec_worker_interface.py`:

- walks every concrete `BaseSpecWorker` subclass (all **7** worker families on main are enumerated: EAGLE, DFlash, NGRAM, DSpark, multi-layer EAGLE, FrozenKVMTP, UNO) and fails if any concrete worker's `forward_batch_generation` cannot accept `pp_proxy_tensors` as a keyword;
- asserts the base-class declaration stays abstract with `batch`/`pp_proxy_tensors` in the signature;
- pins the known worker families so the walk cannot silently miss a module.

**Verified the test bites:** with the worker fixes stashed (test kept), 2 of 3 tests fail exactly on the frozen/uno gaps; with the fixes, 3/3 pass.

## Test Results

- `test/registered/unit/spec/` + `test/registered/unit/speculative/`: **272 passed**. The one collection error in the sweep (`test_dspark_dp_spec_prefill_coordination.py`, `No module named 'deep_gemm'`) is pre-existing on a clean tree — verified by stashing.
- `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` (project pre-commit rules), `ruff format`, `isort`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] I have referenced the issue fixed (#40155).
- [x] I have created at least one test case for the fix.

+"""The scheduler-facing spec-worker contract: ``forward_batch_generation``.
+
+The non-overlap scheduler path always calls the spec worker's
+``forward_batch_generation`` with the ``pp_proxy_tensors`` keyword (None
+unless pipeline parallelism is active). The workers used to diverge on this
+signature one by one, and each divergence only surfaced as
+
+    TypeError: <Worker>.forward_batch_generation() got an unexpected
+    keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'
+
+on the first request through the affected algorithm (issue #40155; the
+FrozenKVMTP and UNO instances were still broken on main). The base class now
+declares the method, and this test walks every concrete ``BaseSpecWorker``
+subclass so the next worker that drops the keyword fails here instead of in
+production.
+"""
+
+import inspect
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+import sglang.srt.speculative.dflash_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+import sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+import sglang.srt.speculative.frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+import sglang.srt.speculative.multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+import sglang.srt.speculative.ngram_worker  # noqa: E402,F401
+import sglang.srt.speculative.uno_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+from sglang.srt.speculative.base_spec_worker import BaseSpecWorker  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.speculative.dspark_components import dspark_worker_v2  # noqa: E402,F401
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _iter_subclasses(cls):
+    for sub in cls.__subclasses__():
+        yield sub
+        yield from _iter_subclasses(sub)
+
+
+def _concrete_spec_workers():
+    for cls in _iter_subclasses(BaseSpecWorker):
+        if not inspect.isabstract(cls):
+            yield cls
+
+
+class TestSpecWorkerForwardBatchGenerationSignature(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_base_class_declares_scheduler_facing_signature(self):
+        """BaseSpecWorker must keep declaring the method abstractly so a new
+        worker that forgets to implement it fails at instantiation."""
+        method = BaseSpecWorker.forward_batch_generation
+        self.assertTrue(
+            getattr(method, "__isabstractmethod__", False),
+            "BaseSpecWorker.forward_batch_generation must stay @abstractmethod",
+        )
+        params = inspect.signature(method).parameters
+        self.assertIn("batch", params)
+        self.assertIn("pp_proxy_tensors", params)
+
+    def test_every_concrete_worker_accepts_pp_proxy_tensors(self):
+        """The non-overlap scheduler calls every worker through
+        ``forward_batch_generation(batch, pp_proxy_tensors=...)``, so any
+        concrete worker missing the keyword dies with a TypeError on its
+        first request (issue #40155)."""
+        workers = list(_concrete_spec_workers())
+        self.assertGreater(
+            len(workers), 0, "expected the worker imports above to register classes"
+        )
+        for cls in workers:
+            with self.subTest(worker=cls.__name__):
+                method = cls.forward_batch_generation
+                self.assertFalse(
+                    getattr(method, "__isabstractmethod__", False),
+                    "concrete spec worker must not stay abstract",
+                )
+                params = inspect.signature(method).parameters
+                self.assertIn(
+                    "pp_proxy_tensors",
+                    params,
+                    "scheduler always passes pp_proxy_tensors (None without PP)",
+                )
+                self.assertIn(
+                    params["pp_proxy_tensors"].kind,
+                    (
+                        inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
+                        inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+                    ),
+                    "pp_proxy_tensors must be passable as a keyword",
+                )
+
+    def test_known_workers_are_covered_by_the_walk(self):
+        """Guard against the walk silently missing modules: every scheduler-
+        facing worker family must appear among the enumerated subclasses."""
+        names = {cls.__name__ for cls in _concrete_spec_workers()}
+        for known in (
+            "EAGLEWorkerV2",
+            "DSparkWorkerV2",
+            "FrozenKVMTPWorkerV2",
+            "NGRAMWorker",
+            "UnoWorkerV2",
+            "MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2",
+            "DFlashWorkerV2",
+        ):
+            self.assertIn(known, names)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
